title: Naturality of etale module pullback under forgetting coefficients
statement: Let X and Y be schemes [def-pc-scheme], f:X→Y a morphism, and Λ a commutative ring. In the categories of constant-coefficient module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] and abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], let U_X and U_Y forget the module structure. There is a natural isomorphism f⁻¹_Mod ⋙ U_X ≅ U_Y ⋙ f⁻¹_Ab, where inverse image is [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. In particular its components commute with every module-sheaf morphism C→F. No finite coefficient, torsion, properness, or henselian hypothesis is required. Unlike an independent choice of objectwise isomorphisms, this single functor isomorphism supplies the commuting square needed on cohomology.

proof.text: The forgetful functor U:ModuleCat Λ→AddCommGrpCat preserves colimits of size u+1, by Mathlib ModuleCat.forget₂PreservesColimitsOfSize. It preserves the limits and covering-sieve colimits in the plus construction, so GrothendieckTopology.instPreservesSheafification gives the sheafification comparison sheafComposeNatIso. All these are natural transformations of functors.

Set L equal to the opposite of the small-etale base-change functor. Preservation of comma-category colimits supplies PreservesPointwiseLeftKanExtensionAt at each object. Since these pointwise Kan extensions exist, preservesPointwiseLKEOfHasPointwiseAndPreservesPointwise supplies preservation of left Kan extensions. Mathlib Functor.lanCompIsoOfPreserves now gives the natural isomorphism L.lan ⋙ whiskeringRight(U) ≅ whiskeringRight(U) ⋙ L.lan.

Unfold upperStar as sheafToPresheaf ⋙ L.lan ⋙ presheafToSheaf. Compose the inverse sheafification comparison with the Kan-extension comparison and whisker by sheafToPresheaf. Insert the associativity isomorphisms of functor composition. The remaining source presheaf functors are definitionally equal, closed by Iso.refl. This constructs one natural isomorphism of the two displayed functors, so its naturality holds for every sheaf morphism. Identity maps, zero rings and empty schemes require no separate choices or extra hypotheses.
